title: Determination SB/007/001/012: mezzanine and extension in a Grade II listed building; travel distance to exit (Requirement B1, section 50(2))
jurisdiction: England (UK): Secretary of State determination / appeal / tribunal under the Building Act 1984 and Building Regulations; comparative test only, not Alberta
code_edition: Building Regulations 2010 (as amended): Requirement B1 (means of warning and escape)
document_date: undated letter; gov.uk index lists it as the latest decision published 24 February 2015

facts.text: The application letter and form are dated 13 November 2014 and enclose plans and drawings; the determination is limited solely to the question put to the Secretary of State.
The approved inspector refused a Plans Certificate on 12 September 2014 because the travel distance of 44 metres from the new mezzanine to the exit was considered an inadequate means of escape.
The building is Grade II listed; construction is stated to have begun around 1450 and to have been completed about 100 years later.

The applicant considers the proposals as they stand comply with requirement B1; the letter says a second spiral stair in the south aisle, to shorten travel distance, is 'wanted neither by the client nor' (the sentence continues in the source).
Determination: the proposals as submitted do not make adequate provision for means of escape in case of fire and do not comply with Requirement B1.
